items.stem: Which best describes self-regulation in emotional intelligence?

options.text: Managing your emotional reactions so you can respond thoughtfully rather than impulsively
options.rationale: Correct: self-regulation is about choosing a considered response, not suppressing feeling.
Regulation does not mean the absence of emotion.

options.text: Hiding all emotions from colleagues permanently
options.rationale: Concealment is not the same as healthy regulation.

options.text: Letting emotions decide every response automatically
options.rationale: That is reactivity, the opposite of regulation.

items.explanation: Correct: self-regulation is about choosing a considered response, not suppressing feeling.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO behaviours demonstrate empathy in a workplace conversation?

options.text: Reflecting back what the other person said to check understanding
options.rationale: Correct: reflective listening confirms you have understood their perspective.

options.text: Attending to tone and non-verbal cues, not only the words
options.rationale: Correct: reading cues helps you grasp how the person actually feels.

options.text: Immediately explaining why their feeling is wrong
options.rationale: Correcting someone's feeling dismisses rather than acknowledges it.

options.text: Changing the subject to your own experience
options.rationale: Redirecting to yourself undercuts attention to the other person.

options.text: Assuming you already know how they feel without checking
options.rationale: Assumption is not empathy; confirming understanding is.

items.explanation: Correct: reflective listening confirms you have understood their perspective.

items.stem: What is a practical benefit of pausing between a trigger and your response?

options.text: It creates space to choose a response aligned with your goals rather than reacting
options.rationale: Correct: the pause lets the thinking brain catch up before you act.

options.text: It guarantees the other person will agree with you
options.rationale: A pause does not control others' agreement.
The emotion remains; the pause changes how you act on it.

options.text: It signals that you are ignoring the issue
options.rationale: A brief pause is not avoidance of the issue.

items.explanation: Correct: the pause lets the thinking brain catch up before you act.
